title: A valid cursor could cause an endless resync: positions come from one installation-wide sequence and project streams have gaps, but a cursor that was no position of the stream, a view's position or 0 included, got cursor-unknown
resolution: A cursor is a boundary of the installation-wide sequence, valid from the retention floor to its head, 0 included; cursor-expired below the floor, cursor-unknown beyond the head; contract page section 10, design decision 16, delta scenarios; a test failed before

title: Recording only the redacted input broke idempotency: two different inputs that redact alike compared equal, and an identical retry could compare unequal
resolution: Repeats compare a keyed digest (HMAC-SHA-256) of the unredacted input, recorded with the key in the outcome's transaction; contract page section 7, design decisions 10 and 18, delta requirement Idempotency before redaction; a test failed before

title: A secret split across two output chunks passed redaction, because each chunk was redacted alone, and successive output-appended events could rebuild it
resolution: A generation's output is redacted as one text: a tail that could still be part of a secret is held back until a later chunk or the generation's end decides it, and reads and events carry only released text; contract page section 7, design decision 18, delta scenario Secret split across output chunks

title: The project stream had no event for Board.workersOnline, so an empty board kept showing no workers online when the first worker came online
resolution: New BoardChangedEvent board-changed in ProjectEvent carries the project and workersOnline as readBoard returns it, also with no cards; contract page section 10, design decision 15, delta scenario; a test failed before

title: The native response requirement answered 409 for every answered request, against the 200 of an idempotent repeat in the document and the contract page
resolution: The requirement answers 200 when the key and response repeat those that answered the request, else 409, and the contract page orders that check before already-answered; scenarios for a lost response and a reused key; a test checks the document's 200 descriptions and failed before

title: The product ports delta rejected every second answer to a resolved item with conflict, also an idempotent repeat with the same key and answer
resolution: The requirement returns the first outcome for the key repeated with the same answer and rejects only another answer or the key with another answer; new scenario Idempotent repeat; product ports section 4.2 says the same

title: The key check and the digest write were not stated atomic with the domain call, so two concurrent commands with one key could both reach the domain and compare redacted text again
resolution: One SERIALIZABLE transaction holds the key check, the domain or source call, and the digest write, the key unique in its scope and a conflict retried as a whole; contract page section 7, design decision 18, requirement Idempotency before redaction, a concurrency scenario

title: Product ports had the source compare a repeated inbox answer, while the contract page resolved repeats before the source, which would compare redacted answers
resolution: The control plane resolves a repeat before NeedsYouSource, which sees only new keys; product ports sections 4.2 and 4.3, the product ports delta with a scenario for a reused key, contract page section 7, design decision 10

title: The subject of a request item named only the native request ID and an ownership generation, so two uncertain deliveries of one reused ID in different generations had equal subjects
resolution: Card subjects carry sessionId and sessionGeneration, required for permission, input, and delivery-acknowledgement items (NativeRequestInboxSubject); CardSubject, product ports section 4.1, contract page sections 8 and 8.1, design decision 19, a requirement, a test that failed before

title: The two answer paths of one input request had different bounds, 65,536 UTF-8 bytes through the inbox and 65,536 UTF-16 code units through the session
resolution: One schema InputAnswerText bounds both paths at MAX_INPUT_ANSWER_BYTES in UTF-8, which implies the MAX_HARNESS_TEXT_LENGTH bound of consumeResponse; contract page sections 8 and 9, design decision 20, requirement One bound for an input answer, a test that failed before

title: The event unions and the stream requirement said every frame's id is its position, which the resync frame contradicts
resolution: The unions, the stream responses, the contract page, and the requirement Event streams except resync and stream-ended, whose frames have no id

title: After a resync the browser's EventSource would reconnect with the same Last-Event-ID and get the same resync, because closing it was not required
resolution: The client closes its EventSource on resync; contract page section 10, ResyncEvent, design decision 16, scenario Expired cursor falls back to snapshots

title: A view read after a resync was said never to get another, which depends on how fast the client reconnects
resolution: Normally gets no other, and a client slower than the retention falls back again; contract page section 10, design decision 16

title: board-changed spoke of the workers online for the project, a qualifier product ports section 3.5 does not give
resolution: The qualifier is removed from BoardChangedEvent, the contract page table, and the scenario

title: Where the held output tail lives and what a restart of the control plane does with it was not stated
resolution: The tail is kept durably with the generation and never shown, and the next chunk or the generation's end, also one recovery records, decides it; contract page sections 7 and 12, design decision 18

title: A session response was not said to resolve the request's inbox item and send its event, so needs-you counts could stay stale
resolution: respondToNativeRequest resolves the item in its transaction and sends inbox-item-changed; contract page section 9, operation description, design decision 9, a scenario

title: Whether an inbox item change also sends its card's card-changed with the new needsYou was not stated
resolution: The same change sends the card's card-changed with its new needsYou; contract page section 10, InboxItemChangedEvent, design decision 15, scenario Item opened for a card

title: Redaction before recording means the harness receives redacted turns and answers, which was not stated, and agent text also covered text a person wrote
resolution: Session text is defined, whoever wrote it, and the consequence for the harness is stated with architecture section 11 on prompts; contract page section 7, design decision 18, requirement Event payloads and session text

title: The fail-before record named the 13 tests of board-session-contracts.test.ts, which held 14 at that commit
resolution: Rerun: 13 of its 14 tests fail, the draft-07 keyword test passes because the schemas are absent; the record says so

title: The record cited needs-you.ts:26 at ff7ab7a0, a line no file of the change cites
resolution: The citation is removed from the record

title: Tests of the pass 1 fixes matched description prose rather than the schemas
resolution: The tests check the resync reasons, the cursor parameter schemas, and the success schemas of repeated commands; the rules stay prose on the contract page

title: The draft-07 keyword test missed dynamic and recursive references and contains bounds, and did not check keywords beside a reference
resolution: The test lists those keywords and checks that a reference has at most a description beside it
